standard.title: Discuss perspectives on places and events
standard.description: discuss perspectives related to objects, people, places and events
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y1 (AC9HS1S04): Students compared perspectives across generations and shared personal preferences about places and events with reasons.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students discuss perspectives related to objects, people, places and events, including perspectives of different community groups.

nodes.label: Why places are significant to different groups
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discuss why some places are considered special or significant by different groups (parents, First Nations Australians, grandparents, friends, returned soldiers) and explain why significance differs.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain why the same place is significant to at least two different people or groups, identifying what makes it significant for each.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss why some places are special to parents, First Nations Australians, grandparents, elders, friends and returned soldiers; explore how the same place has significance to different groups for different reasons.
wider: Investigate traditional meeting places for First Nations Australians within an urban area and compare their significance with that of nearby buildings or monuments important to other cultural groups
Interview two different people about the same local place and compare their perspectives on why it matters

response_modes.reason: Multiple perspectives on the same place are more powerful than multiple perspectives on different places — use a single local site to anchor diverse perspective comparison.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: A single significant local place seen through multiple group lenses — First Nations, returned soldiers, cultural communities — models genuine historical perspective-taking in a concrete, local context.
success_criteria: Explains why at least two different groups find the same place significant
Describes at least one reason why significance differs between groups

nodes.label: Older generations' perspectives on change
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can examine points of view of older generations about changes over time to the natural or built environment or to daily living.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one point of view an older person holds about a change they have witnessed in their lifetime.
nodes.typical_width: Examine perspectives of older generations on changes to the natural or built environment and daily living; compare with students' own perspectives on the same changes; discuss how experience shapes perspective.
wider: Compare perspectives on the same change from two people of different generations and explain what shaped each view
Discuss how perspectives on a change can be positive for one group and negative for another

response_modes.reason: Perspectives on change integrate historical knowledge of what changed with empathetic understanding of how people experienced that change — the integration of history and perspective-taking.

success_criteria: Describes at least one point of view an older person holds about change
Compares that view with their own perspective on the same change
